items.title: NovoAtlas
items.text:
Welcome to the NovoAtlas wiki! NovoAtlas is a prescribed Minecraft world generator, based on the original Atlas mod by itsmiir. This mod allows you to paint a world's height map and biome map, and then import that to a datapack and allow the Minecraft world generator to fill in the rest of the details!

Tip

All information on this wiki is for the latest version of Minecraft by default. If you are on an older version, please select it at the top of the screen to get information for your specific version.

items.title: Player Support
items.text: If you're having trouble with the mod, you can join my Discord and make a post in the #help-and-support forum. For help with the original Atlas mod, join itmiir's Discord.

items.title: Minecraft Version Support
items.text: See https://www.thedeathlycow.com/novoatlas/#lts-policy for the current version support policy.

items.title: How to Create a NovoAtlas Dimension
items.text:
1. Create or find a grayscale image height map in one of the supported formats. You may either use 8-bit RGB or 16-bit grayscale, if your image format supports it. To create maps, I would highly recommend using WorldPainter, as it is purpose-built for Minecraft map making and has an option to export a height map. You can also get heightmaps of Earth from a variety of websites, here's a few that I've found (though not tested with NovoAtlas):
    • https://tangrams.github.io/heightmapper/
    • https://visibleearth.nasa.gov/images/73934/topography
    • https://heightmap.skydark.pl/ (Requires a Mapbox API key)
  2. Create a copy of the map and paint over it with whatever colours you like. Each colour corresponds to a different biome. Do not mix or blend the colours. Save this image as one of the supported formats with 8-bit RGBA encoding. For cave biomes, you can create separate maps for each "layer" of the world.
  3. Create a datapack and add these images to it, you can either copy one of the example datapacks or make one from scratch yourself.

items.title: Examples
items.text: The Example Datapacks are builtin with NovoAtlas and can be selected on world creation. You can also download them separately from the GitHub releases page.

items.title: Modifying a NovoAtlas Dimension
items.text:
Note

Modifying dimensions requires that you already know how to configure datapacks. If you have never done this before, the Minecraft Wiki has a basic overview (there are also tutorials on YouTube).

You can of course, create or modify a NovoAtlas by yourself too. This is mainly done through the new datapack registry novoatlas/map_info. The full format of map info objects can be found here. The height map and biome map images have separate registries, novoatlas/heightmap and novoatlas/biome_map respectively.

Once you have your map info, you will need to create or modify a dimension. The actual generation of the map is done with a custom chunk generator (format) and custom biome source (format).

items.title: Some Tips
items.text:
• The easiest way to create a NovoAtlas datapack is to copy an example back from the releases page of NovoAtlas and replace the height and biome maps with your own. Your biome map should be ¼ the width and height of your heightmap for them to match.
  • When you're drawing the biomes, it may be helpful to be able to see the heightmap as a contour map. You can emulate this in your preferred photo editor by selecting a black pixel and then using "select by colour" with varying thresholds to get varying contour lines of your map.
  • Your map will be centred at (0, 0), unless you supply an offset. Up in the image is north. If your map is an uneven number of pixels, the last pixel on the south and/or east side will be cut off.
  • If you use 16-bit-per-color heightmap images to allow for heightmap values outside the 256 block range1, and you are getting a flat world at y=320, try using the vertical scale option in the map info format to reduce the final heights of the map to more sensible Minecraft values. For example, in maps that use the full 16-bit range, a vertical scale of 320 / 65535 = 0.004882887 works well.
  • When creating large maps, you can use the horizontal_scale option to increase the size of the world from smaller images, which will save RAM and disk space. The default interpolation strategy will produce rather blocky results, but you can also try using other interpolation types as specified in the map info format.
  • To allow for lakes and rivers at varying heights from sea level, use the fluid_height_map option of the map info. This is a separate map to your regular terrain that tells the game what level to generate the dimension's default fluid at (normally water). If two different fluid levels meet and there is not land to separate them, then the game will try to generate barriers between them, like aquifers do.
  • The mod Worldgen Devtools can be helpful for advanced development and debugging.

  1. Like this one. ↩

items.title: Biome Sources
items.text: These are alternative formats for the biome_source field present within the chunk generator field of the dimension definition. This is not a new registry, you must edit files with the dimension registry.

items.title: Biome Cell Color Map
items.text:
This biome source maps each pixel of your biome map images to a biome cell, which is a 4x4 section of blocks. Therefore, each pixel in your image will correspond to 16 blocks square.

  • {} biome_source: The parent tag in the novoatlas chunk generator.
    • " type: Must be set to novoatlas:biome_cell_color_map for this biome source to apply.
    • " map_info: A resource location of the map info object to use.
    • " default_biome: The biome to use for unmapped colors.

items.title: Bounded Map Biome Cell Color Map
items.text:
Warning

This object is considered experimental, meaning its format could change in future updates. As such, it uses the namespace novoatlas-experimental!

This biome source works like biome cell source, except that it allows for a secondary generator to apply outside the bounds of its image and attempts to blend between them as best it can. The biome cells inside of the map will match exactly as the image prescribes it to be, only the cells outside of the map boundaries will be blended.

  • {} biome_source: The parent tag in the novoatlas chunk generator.
    • " type: Must be set to novoatlas-experimental:bounded_biome_cell_color_map for this biome source to apply.
    • " map_info: A resource location of the map info object to use.
    • " default_biome: The biome to use for unmapped colors.
    • {} outside_map: Another biome source, either a NovoAtlas biome source or a vanilla one, to be used outside the bounds of the map.

items.title: Color Map
items.text:
Warning

This generator is deprecated, and has been replaced by the biome cell source.

This biome source maps each pixel of your biome map images to a single block. Therefore, each pixel in your image will correspond to 1 block. Because Minecraft actually uses cells to place biomes, this will cause almost all pixels in the image to be unused. For this reason it is highly recommended to use the biome cell source instead.

  • {} biome_source: The parent tag in the novoatlas chunk generator.
    • " type: Must be set to novoatlas:color_map for this biome source to apply.
    • " map_info: A resource location of the map info object to use.
    • " default_biome: The biome to use for unmapped colors.

items.title: Examples
items.text: See the biome sources in the Chunk generator examples.

items.title: Chunk Generators
items.text: These are alternative formats for the generator field present within the Dimension definition. This is not a new registry, you must edit files with the dimension registry.

items.title: Image Map
items.text:
This generator is a variant of minecraft:multi_noise that will modify the final_density and preliminary_surface_level density functions in the provided noise settings' noise router with its own density functions that read from the heightmap to determine noise values. The preliminary_surface_level will be fully replaced, and the final_density will use the minimum density value of the heightmap and the original final density function.

  • {} generator: The parent tag in a custom dimension.
    • " type: Must be set to novoatlas:image_map for this generator to apply.
    • " map_info: A resource location of the map info object to use.
    • " settings: A resource location of the noise settings to use. Usually, you will want this to be something like minecraft:overworld.
    • " underground_density_function: A resource location of a density function to use. Can be any density function, but using one of novoatlas:caves or novoatlas:no_caves is recommended.
    • {} biome_source: The biome source to use. Can be any biome source, but using the color map biome source is highly recommended.
    • T/F enable_carvers: Optional boolean, defaults to true. A simple toggle for whether to disable all carvers (the old type of caves).

items.title: Blend Image To Random
items.text:
Warning

This object is considered experimental, meaning its format could change in future updates. As such, it uses the namespace novoatlas-experimental!

This works similarly to novoatlas:image_map, except that outside the bounds of the map it will blend the image's height values to the random values provided by the settings field. The terrain inside of the map will match exactly as the image prescribes it to be, only the blocks outside of the map boundaries will be blended.

  • {} generator: The parent tag in a custom dimension.
    • " type: Must be set to novoatlas-experimental:blend_image_map_to_random for this generator to apply.
    • " map_info: A resource location of the map info object to use.
    • " settings: A resource location of the noise settings to use. Usually, you will want this to be something like minecraft:overworld.
    • " underground_density_function: A resource location of a density function to use. Can be any density function, but using one of novoatlas:caves or novoatlas:no_caves is recommended.
    • {} biome_source: The biome source to use. Can be any biome source, but using the color map biome source is highly recommended.
    • T/F enable_carvers: Optional boolean, defaults to true. A simple toggle for whether to disable all carvers (the old type of caves).
    • F32 blend_distance: Optional 32-bit float, defaults to 64.0. Must be greater than 0. This is the distance over which the blending will apply in blocks.

items.title: Examples
items.text:
A basic dimension definition to override the vanilla Overworld.

avila-basic-example/data/minecraft/dimension/overworld.json
{
    "type": "minecraft:overworld",
    "generator": { // (1)!
        "type": "novoatlas:image_map",
        "map_info": "avila-example:avila",
        "settings": "minecraft:overworld",
        "underground_density_function": "novoatlas:caves",
        "biome_source": { // (2)!
            "type": "novoatlas:biome_cell_color_map",
            "map_info": "avila-example:avila",
            "default_biome": "minecraft:the_void"
        }
    }
}
  1. This is the parent tag for the chunk generator.
  2. This can be any biome source.

A custom dimension that blends the image-based, prescribed terrain to a random overworld-like terrain.

avila-blend-to-random-example/data/avila-random-example/dimension/avila.json
{
    "type": "minecraft:overworld",
    "generator": {
        "type": "novoatlas-experimental:blend_image_map_to_random",
        "map_info": "avila-random-example:avila",
        "settings": "minecraft:overworld",
        "underground_density_function": "novoatlas:caves",
        "blend_distance": 256,
        "biome_source": {
            "type": "novoatlas-experimental:bounded_biome_cell_color_map",
            "map_info": "avila-random-example:avila",
            "default_biome": "minecraft:the_void",
            "blend_distance": 64,
            "outside_map": {
                "type": "minecraft:multi_noise",
                "preset": "minecraft:overworld"
            }
        }
    }
}

items.title: Density Functions
items.text:
These are additional types of density functions supplied by NovoAtlas. These can be used in any density_function registry entry or in-line where density functions are required in other things like noise routers.

For most users, you should never need to worry about these when using NovoAtlas. The mod automatically applies them to your chunk generators (which is why some of the formats are a bit messy for normal datapack development).

items.title: Heightmap
items.text:
Using a heightmap in a map info, computes positive density below the surface and negative density above the surface, with some blending in between.

  • {}: The parent tag.
    • " type: Must be set to novoatlas:heightmap for this density function to apply.
    • " map_info: A resource location of the map info object to use for the heightmap data.
    • F32 transition_range: Optional 32 bit float, defaults to 10. Specifies how wide the density values should interpolate above/below the surface.

items.title: Get Height From Map
items.text:
Returns the raw height value from a heightmap in a map info.

  • {}: The parent tag.
    • " type: Must be set to novoatlas:get_height_from_map for this density function to apply.
    • " map_info: A resource location of the map info object to use for the heightmap data.
    • F32 lower_bound: A 32 bit float between -2032 and 2031 (inclusive). Clamps the minimum height to this value.
    • F32 upper_bound: A 32 bit float between -2032 and 2031 (inclusive). Clamps the maximum height to this value.

items.title: Get Preliminary Height From Map
items.text:
Does the exact same thing like as Get Height From Map, but subtracts the height value by 8 to allow it to be used as a preliminary height in the noise router.

  • {}: The parent tag.
    • " type: Must be set to novoatlas:get_preliminary_height_from_map for this density function to apply.
    • " map_info: A resource location of the map info object to use for the heightmap data.
    • F32 lower_bound: A 32 bit float between -2032 and 2031 (inclusive). Clamps the minimum height to this value.
    • F32 upper_bound: A 32 bit float between -2032 and 2031 (inclusive). Clamps the maximum height to this value.

items.title: Blend At Map Border
items.text:
Warning

This object is considered experimental, meaning its format could change in future updates. As such, it uses the namespace novoatlas-experimental!

This density function is used to blend two other density functions together based on the boundaries of a map. It is intended to be used as the final density for blend-to-random generation. Around the boundary of the map, it will blend the raw density values together using a smoothstep function.

  • {}: The parent tag.
    • " type: Must be set to novoatlas-experimental:blend_at_map_border for this density function to apply.
    • " map_info: A resource location of the map info object to use to determine the boundaries of the map.
    • " {} inside_map: The density function to use when generating inside the map. This should supply the final density for blocks inside the map.
    • " {} outside_map: The density function to use when generating outside the map. This should supply the final density for blocks outside the map.
    • F32 blend_distance: An 32-bit float. Must be greater than 0. How far, in blocks, to blend the two inside/out map functions using the preliminary surface level.

items.title: Images
items.text:
In NovoAtlas, all images are supplied via datapacks in a one of two custom registries: novoatlas/heightmap or novoatlas/biome_map. Heightmaps can be any grayscale image, and it supports both 8-bit and 16-bit grayscale PNG images. Biome maps can be any 8 bit-per-channel RGB image.

You may supply images as .png, .jpg,.jpeg, .tif, .tiff, .wbp, .bmp, .gif, .wbmp, or .webp. While some of these formats support lossy compression, this will almost certainly lead to issues in NovoAtlas. Therefore, it is highly recommended that users stick to .png where possible, or disable all lossy compression otherwise. These images are fully decompressed when loaded into memory, so you would not gain much from having high lossy compression anyway.

Also, if two images in the same registry have the same path/name, but different formats, then one will override the other. For example, you cannot have novoatlas/heightmap/avila.png and novoatlas/heightmap/avila.webp at the same time; you must pick one.

items.title: Map Info
items.text:
This is the central registry of NovoAtlas. It is responsible for managing all the images for your world, basically everything comes through here.

Tip

All Map Info entries go in the novoatlas/map_info registry in your datapack. For example, data/my-awesome-datapack/novoatlas/map_info/my_awesome_world.json.

  • {}: The root tag.
    • " height_map: The resource location of the height map to use, must be a black and white image in the registry novoatlas/heightmap.
    • " fluid_height_map: Optional. The resource location of the fluid height map to use, must be a black and white image in the registry novoatlas/heightmap. If not specified, the world's regular sea level will be used.
    • I32 starting_y: Tells the game how high the lowest block in the heightmap should be. I.e., the elevation that a black pixel on the heightmap represents in-game.
    • [] center_offset: An optional list of 2 floats that offsets the center position of the map. The units are in [width, height] respectively, NOT in blocks. Defaults to [0, 0].
    • " image_wrapping: Optional enumerated string that specifies a mode for how to wrap the map image beyond the borders of the central image. Valid values are clamp_to_edge, repeat, and mirrored_repeat. Defaults to clamp_to_edge.
    • {} surface_biomes: A biome color provider containing information about the surface biomes. See below for format.
    • {} cave_biomes: An optional compound containing information about the cave biomes. If left empty, no cave biomes will generate.
      • [] layers: A list of biome layer entries that describes what cave biomes to generate (roughly) at each y-level.
    • I32 surface_range: Optional integer, defaults to 16. The depth below the surface of the heightmap that cave biomes should begin spawning, if any cave biomes are specified.
    • {} scaling: A scale configuration compound
      • F32 vertical_scale: An optional positive float that multiplies the heightmap values, allowing for the height to be increased or decreased. Useful for 16-bits-per-color images. Defaults to 1.0.
      • F32 horizontal_scale: An optional positive float that multiplies the size of the map. When specified as a float, will use nearest_neighbor interpolation. Defaults to 1.0.
      • {} horizontal_scale: The horizontal scale can alternatively be specified as an optional compound, allowing for configuration of the interpolation strategy.
        • F32 value: A positive float that multiplies the size of the map.
        • " interpolation: A resource location identifying the interpolation type to use, to allow for smooth blending between pixel values (especially with large values). Must be one of the Interpolation Types. Defaults to novoatlas:nearest_neighbor.
        • Additional fields, depending on the value of interpolation.

Note

The cave biomes layers list will only use the first entry in this list to match a given y value.

items.title: Biome Layer Entry
items.text:
• {}: The root tag.
    • {} y_range: The range at which to place this layer.
      • I32 min: Optional integer, the minimum y-range to place this layer at. Must be strictly less than max.
      • I32 max: Optional integer, the maximum y-range to place this layer at.
    • {} biomes: A biome color provider containing information about this layer's biomes. See below for format.

Tip

Having a layer use the special biome type novoatlas:surface_biome in its color provider will cause the generator to place the surface biome at that (x, z) position in the layer.

items.title: Biome Color Provider
items.text:
• {}: The root tag.
  • " map: The resource location of the biome map to use, must be a colour image in the registry novoatlas/biome_map.
  • T/F strict: Optional boolean. Whether to be strict in the mapping of colours to biomes. If true, then the default biome of the parent biome source will be used when a colour that is not defined in the biomes list is sampled in the map. Otherwise, the closest colour (based on RGB vector distance) is used instead. Defaults to false.
  • [] biomes: A list that maps colors in the biome map image to actual biomes. Each color may ONLY APPEAR ONCE in this list! List entries are of the following format:
    • {}: The root tag.
    • " biome: The resource location of the biome this color maps to.
    • I32 ": An 8-bit RGB color value, may be either an integer or a string. If an unquoted integer, then must be a decimal representation of the RGB color value. If a quoted string, then it must be a #-prefixed RGB color hex code. More formally, this string must match the regular expression #[0-9a-fA-F]{6}. That means a string must be of the form #XXXXXX where X is a hexadecimal digit.

items.title: Interpolation Types
items.text:
NovoAtlas provides a registry for interpolation types. Third-party mods can register new codecs to this registry to provide new values, however NovoAtlas provides a few built in. You may choose any one of the following types:

From my testing, the nearest neighbor works well for horizontal scales from 0-1, bilinear works well for scales from 1-2, bicubic works well for scales 2-5, and lanczos works well for scales over 5 (depending on the window size). However, bicubic and lanczos can require more CPU power to run, lanczos in particular will be quite slow with large window sizes.

  • {} horizontal_scale: The root tag.

    • " interpolation: If novoatlas:nearest_neighbor or minecraft:nearest_neighbor or nearest_neighbor, will use a simple blocky interpolation. This is the default strategy. Has no additional fields.

  • {} horizontal_scale: The root tag.

    • " interpolation: If novoatlas:bilinear or minecraft:bilinear or bilinear, will use a linearly interpolated smoothing that eliminates blockiness for large scaling values but is still somewhat jagged. Has no additional fields.

  • {} horizontal_scale: The root tag.

    • " interpolation: If novoatlas:bicubic or minecraft:bicubic or bicubic, will use a cubic interpolated smoothing that is less jagged than bilinear but has worse performance and will still produce noticeable artefacts at large scaling values. Has no additional fields.

  • {} horizontal_scale: The root tag.

    • " interpolation: If novoatlas:lanczos or minecraft:lanczos or lanczos, will use Lánczos interpolated smoothing that produces better results than bilinear and bicubic for very large scaling values but has generally the same or much worse performance, depending on the size of the window.
    • I32 window: Optional positive 32-bit integer. Specifies the window size of the interpolation. Higher values may produce better, but very quickly increases CPU load. Defaults to 2.

items.title: Examples
items.text:
A simple map info from the Avila Basic Example datapack.

data/avila-example/novoatlas/map_info/avila.json

            "interpolation": "nearest_neighbor"
